purpose: Demeclocycline is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as respiratory tract infections, urinary tract infections, and skin infections. It is also sometimes used to treat a condition called SIADH, where the body holds too much water and the sodium level in the blood drops too low.
how_it_works: This medicine works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Without those proteins, the bacteria cannot survive and spread. This gives your immune system a better chance to fight off the infection.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, and diarrhea. You may also notice increased sensitivity to sunlight, which means your skin can burn more easily than usual. Some people experience dizziness or headache.
warnings: Avoid prolonged sun or UV light exposure while taking this medication — always use sunscreen and protective clothing. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm a developing baby or infant's teeth and bones. Do not give it to children under 8 years old for the same reason. Take it with a full glass of water and avoid lying down for at least 30 minutes after taking it to prevent irritation of the esophagus. Dairy products, antacids, and iron supplements can reduce how well this medicine works, so try to take it on an empty stomach.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 150 mg taken four times a day, or 300 mg taken twice a day. Your doctor will adjust the dose depending on your specific condition. Always take the full course of antibiotics even if you start feeling better early.
